name: Tessek Black Sesame-Honey Bark
manufacturer: Tessek Foods (Corponation subsidiary of Nalvec Consumer Goods)
description: Thin snappable slabs of synth-cocoa bark studded with toasted black sesame and a honey-analog glaze. Tessek positions this as an 'artisanal adjacent' product — corporate scale, craft presentation, mid-tier price.
flavor_profile: Bitter synth-cocoa base, nutty roasted sesame, floral honey sweetness, slight waxy finish that distinguishes it from real chocolate
cultural_context: The snap of a Tessek bark slab has become a minor social ritual — sharing pieces across a table signals a casual truce or a relaxed meeting. In Tier 3 offices, leaving a slab on someone's desk is a soft apology. The product's modest success has spawned a dozen knockoff bark brands, most inferior.
story_hooks: A corporate negotiator always places Tessek bark on the table before difficult meetings — except today they forgot, and their counterpart reads it as an intentional slight.
A street chemist has figured out how to infuse unlicensed stim compounds into the honey glaze without affecting appearance or snap — the supply chain is compromised from a mid-level Tessek warehouse.
The sesame in a recent batch came from a contaminated synth-farm; Nalvec's suppression of the quality report is about to leak.
